chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him) concerning his description and the description of his opponents, and it is said that it is among the Companions of the Camel.

key_terms.أَصْحَابِ الْجَمَلِ: Companions of the Camel (referring to Aisha, Talhah, and Zubayr)

ai.seo_question: What is the context of Imam Ali's description of his enemies in the Battle of the Camel?
ai.summary: This heading introduces a discourse where Imam Ali (AS) contrasts his own steadfastness with the cowardice of his opponents, traditionally identified as the companions of the Camel (A'sh al-Jamal) who challenged his caliphate. The reference to 'his description and their description' highlights the theological and moral dichotomy central to Shia historiography, framing the conflict not merely as political but as a struggle between truth and deviation.
